turns.t: G'day, you're Chloe Nakamura, yeah? Just checking I've got the right file open.
Yes, that's me. Hi, doctor. Sorry, I'm a bit nervous. I've been googling and it's all gone a bit dark.
Ha, Dr Google has never helped anyone sleep. Tell me what's been happening.
I'm gaining weight and I don't know why. I'm eating the same as always, if anything less.
How much are we talking about, and over how long?
About six kilos, I think? But when did it start... I honestly can't say. Maybe winter, maybe before that.
Not knowing is fine. Lots of people only notice when their jeans stop doing up. Has anything changed at work or home?
I work night shifts at the hospital, a few months now. Everything's upside down.
That can muddle your body clock. Your file says you take a thyroid tablet. Remind me what it's for?
For my underactive thyroid. Levothyroxine, 75 micrograms, once a day, every morning before breakfast.
Good. And you take it every single day?
Yes, every morning. Well, most mornings. On night-shift days I honestly can't tell if I've taken it. I worry I've doubled up or missed it.
That's very common, and we'll sort it. Think of the thyroid as the thermostat in a house. If the heater's patchy, the whole place runs cool and slow.
So that could explain the weight?
It could. Let me ask about the rest of you. How are your bowels?
Fine. Regular as clockwork, oddly.
Good. Any pounding heart or palpitations, or feeling shaky?
No palpitations. Nothing like that.
Okay. Any allergies I should have on file before we go further?
Yes, actually, that's something I wanted to ask. I'm allergic to penicillin. I came out in hives when I was about twenty.
That's well worth having on the file. And your thyroid tablet is nothing like penicillin, so there's no clash there.
What if I need an antibiotic one day? Will they know?
It's flagged on your record, so any prescriber will see it, and I'd remind them anyway. Penicillin, hives. Remember those two words.
Okay, that helps. Can an allergy like that fade over time?
Sometimes, yes. Plenty of people grow out of a penicillin reaction, and there are proper ways to test it if it ever matters. For now, we treat it as real.
Right. Can we do the checks now? I'd like to know I'm not falling apart.
Righto. Pressure, pulse and weight first, then I'll feel your neck.
Pressure is 124 over 78, pulse 62, and weight 82 kilograms.
Eighty-two? Is that terrible?
It's a number, not a verdict. It matches what you're telling me. Now chin up, I'll feel your thyroid.
Thyroid feels normal in size and smooth. Nothing odd there.
Is that good? Could it be cancer? Sorry, I had to ask.
Nothing I felt points that way. In plain English, I think this is most likely your underactive thyroid not being fully covered, probably because of the patchy doses.
So I wasn't imagining it. Can't you just put the dose up?
Not yet. A bigger dose on top of missed ones just makes a rollercoaster. First, lock in the routine. Phone alarm, tablet next to the toothbrush, same time even after a night shift.
Okay. An alarm. I can do an alarm.
And give it half an hour on its own before your coffee or breakfast.
Thank you, doctor. I feel much less scared now.
Good on you. Look after yourself, and try to catch some sleep.
I will. Thanks again.

physical_examination.finding: Thyroid feels normal in size and smooth

clinical_assessment.assessment: your underactive thyroid not being fully covered

clinical_actions.description: Take levothyroxine at the same time daily using a phone alarm, half an hour before coffee or breakfast

clinical_uncertainties.description: The patient cannot say when the weight gain started.
The patient says she takes levothyroxine every morning but is unsure on night-shift days whether she has taken it.
